newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says unimportant if Brady closing Dec or Jan.
newsitem.headline: Peru says unimportant if Brady closing Dec or Jan.

text.p: Peru's Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress Wednesday it was not important whether the country formally closed its Brady plan deal with commercial creditors in December or January.
"I do not think it has much importance whether the Brady (accord) closes in December or January," Camet said. "What is best for us is that we reconcile the figures more precisely," he added.
The government was due to confirm last Friday a December 20 date for the closing of the deal.
However, economy ministry sources said they did not make the announcement because the governmenment wanted to wait until it was sure everything was in place for the closing.
There were still many "mechanical processes" to finalize before the closing, according to one economy ministry source.

Previously, Economy Ministry officials have said the precise financing of the Brady deal, and the "reconciliation" of some interest, or agreement with bank creditors on exactly how much interest is owed, were the main points still to finalized in the plan.

Earlier this month the government signed a preliminary Brady bond debt accord with its commercial creditors containing most of the final details for the restructuring of $4.4 billion of principal and interest.

The government has said that 180 commercial creditors, accounting for 99 percent of the debt included in the agreement, had selected one or more of the options available in the plan, which include Discount bonds, Par bonds, Front-Loaded Interest Rate bonds (Flirbs) and debt buyback.
However, Peruvian officials have said they want to reduce Flirbs to 40 percent or less and would prefer increasing the Discounts to around 25 percent.
-- Saul Hudson, Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
